frames.narration: An engineer changes the payments timeout from 800 ms to 500 ms for production and submits it for review. The change is not live yet: it is a proposal against version 42.

The schema check confirms that timeout_ms is an integer between 50 and 5,000 and that the retry budget still fits inside the new timeout. The store saves it as version 43, an immutable record with the author and a checksum. Version 42 is kept.
The rollout controller starts stage 1. It marks 5% of the 2,000 payment instances, which is 100, as the group that receives version 43. The other 1,900 stay on version 42.

One of the 100 instances polls. It sends the version it holds, so the API answers with version 43 and its checksum. The instance verifies the checksum and the schema, writes the file to disk as the new copy, and applies it.

The controller watches the health metrics for five minutes. The error rate of the 100 instances is 0.1%, the same as the 1,900 others, so the gate passes. It repeats the steps at 25%, which is 500 instances, and then at 100%.

Version 43 is now the stable version everywhere, and the audit trail shows who changed what, who approved it and when each stage started. Rolling back would mean pointing the stable version at 42 again.

Later the config service is down while this instance restarts. The instance cannot fetch anything, so it reads the last-known-good copy from its disk, version 43, and starts normally. It keeps retrying with backoff and jitter until the service returns.
